mainTopic: What counts as שגגה for a קרבן or חומש, how a lost traveler keeps שבת, and the source for the משנה's rules on forgetting שבת
overview: This amud opens by finishing אביי's claim that, for a false oath about the past (שבועת ביטוי לשעבר), not knowing about the קרבן is not enough to count as שגגה. A ברייתא challenges him. In one version the גמרא assigns the ברייתא to מונבז; in another version that answer is rejected, and אביי is refuted. Next, אביי rules that a person pays the extra fifth (חומש) for eating תרומה only if he did not know the prohibition itself, and רבא disagrees. Then a new topic begins: how a traveler who lost track of the days keeps שבת. רב הונא says count six days and then keep one, and חייא בר רב says the reverse; two ברייתות refute חייא בר רב. רבא adds that the traveler does only enough work each day to eat, marks his chosen שבת with קידוש and הבדלה, and may work fully on the weekday he set out. Finally, the גמרא returns to the משנה and learns the difference between one who forgot the עיקר שבת and one who knows it from two פסוקים, one singular and one plural. It then quotes the משנה's next case, one who knows that it is שבת.

steps.title: Closing line: אביי's teaching is a real חידוש
steps.stepSummary: The tail of the previous answer: אביי is teaching us that even רבי יוחנן requires שגגה in the prohibition itself for a false oath about the past.
steps.simpleTranslation: So אביי comes to teach us that it is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of an answer that started on the previous section. The גמרא is closing the point that אביי's statement teaches something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the גמרא said one might think: since a קרבן for שבועת ביטוי is unusual (a חידוש), not knowing about the קרבן should count as שגגה even though there is no כרת. 'קא משמע לן' says אביי rejects that. Even רבי יוחנן agrees that one must be unaware of the prohibition itself.

keyTerms.meaning: He teaches us (this is the new point)
An oath on a personal statement ("I swear I ate / did not eat")

phrases.english: He teaches us (that it is not so).
phrases.notes: This wraps up the 'you might have thought' (מהו דתימא) answer that started on the previous amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer earlier explaining why אביי's 'הכל מודים' is not obvious.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the statement teaches a non-obvious point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the קרבן of שבועת ביטוי is a חידוש, ignorance of the קרבן alone might count as שגגה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even רבי יוחנן requires שגגה in the actual prohibition for a false oath about the past.

steps.title: A ברייתא says not knowing about the קרבן is enough
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines שגגה for a false oath about the past as knowing it is forbidden but not knowing that it brings a קרבן. This contradicts אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: What is an unwitting false oath about the past? If he said, 'I know this oath is forbidden, but I do not know whether one must bring a קרבן for it,' he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to attack אביי. The ברייתא calls someone who only did not know about the קרבן a שוגג, and he is liable to bring a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said that everyone, even רבי יוחנן, requires ignorance of the prohibition itself for this oath. The ברייתא describes a person who knew the prohibition and still calls him liable. So for this oath, 'שגגת קרבן' seems to be enough, which directly contradicts אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacrifice (here a sin-offering for an unwitting sin)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
What is an unwitting oath on a statement about the past?
That if he said, 'I know
that this oath is forbidden,
but I do not know

phrases.aramaic: אִם חַיָּיבִין עָלֶיהָ קׇרְבָּן אוֹ לֹא״ —
phrases.english: whether one is liable to bring a sacrifice for it or not' —
he is liable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the teaching of אביי that was just established.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that everyone requires שגגה in the prohibition for שבועת ביטוי לשעבר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא makes a person liable even though he knew the prohibition and only did not know about the קרבן.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows מונבז
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is assigned to מונבז, who holds that שגגת קרבן counts as שגגה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is מונבז.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the ברייתא reflects the view of מונבז alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מונבז holds that throughout the Torah, not knowing about the קרבן counts as שגגה. The ברייתא simply applies his general rule. אביי's 'everyone agrees' referred to רבי יוחנן and the רבנן, not to מונבז, so a ברייתא that follows מונבז does not contradict אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: מונבז, a תנא who holds that ignorance of the קרבן counts as שגגה

phrases.english: Whose view is this?
It is מונבז.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by assigning the ברייתא to a specific תנא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to a particular opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא states the universal rule and refutes אביי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows מונבז's general view that שגגת קרבן is שגגה.

steps.title: Second version: the ברייתא cannot be מונבז, because that would be obvious
steps.stepSummary: In another version, the גמרא rejects attributing the ברייתא to מונבז. If מונבז says this everywhere, he surely says it for the unusual case of שבועת ביטוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Another version: Whose view is it? If you say מונבז, that is obvious! Throughout the Torah, where the קרבן is not unusual, he said that not knowing about the קרבן counts as שגגה. Here, where it is unusual, all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a second version of the discussion, in which the answer 'it is מונבז' does not work. It sets up the conclusion that the ברייתא must follow the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מונבז already holds that שגגת קרבן is שגגה for ordinary sins. The קרבן of שבועת ביטוי is a special חידוש, so it carries even more weight. A ברייתא that only taught מונבז's view would add nothing new, so it is unlikely to be his.

keyTerms.meaning: A novelty; an unusual law that goes beyond the normal pattern
Is it not all the more so?

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument after step 3. It is a different version of the same exchange, in which the 'מונבז' answer fails.

phrases.english: (Another version:
Whose view is it?
If you say מונבז — that is obvious,
now, throughout the entire Torah
where it is not a novelty,
he said unwitting regarding a sacrifice is called unwitting;
here, where it is a novelty,
is it not all the more so?!

steps.triggerLanguage: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא: מַנִּי? אִילֵּימָא מוֹנְבַּז — פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative version that undermines the answer in step 3.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By קל וחומר, מונבז would obviously hold this. A ברייתא saying only that would be pointless.

steps.title: So the ברייתא is the רבנן, and אביי is refuted
steps.stepSummary: Since the ברייתא cannot be מונבז, it must follow the רבנן. Then even the רבנן accept שגגת קרבן here, which contradicts אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not the רבנן? Then this is a refutation of אביי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the result of the second version. The ברייתא follows the רבנן, so אביי's 'everyone agrees' is contradicted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even the רבנן, who normally reject שגגת קרבן, accept it for שבועת ביטוי, then the claim that 'everyone' requires ignorance of the prohibition here is false.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not the Rabbis,
and it is a refutation of אביי!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו רַבָּנַן הִיא, וּתְיוּבְתָּא דְאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the argument started in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's 'הכל מודים' about שבועת ביטוי לשעבר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא, now attributed to the רבנן, accepts שגגת קרבן for this oath.

steps.title: The refutation stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concedes that אביי is refuted, according to the second version.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a refutation.)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that אביי's statement is rejected in this version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No answer is offered, so אביי's claim about שבועת ביטוי falls in the second version. In the first version it survived by assigning the ברייתא to מונבז.
steps.whatToRemember: In one version, the ברייתא is assigned to מונבז, so it says nothing about the רבנן. In the other, that assignment is rejected as obvious, so the ברייתא must be the רבנן's, and אביי is explicitly refuted: for שבועת ביטוי, even the רבנן count ignorance of the קרבן as שגגה.

phrases.english: It is a refutation.)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the refutation from step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to the second version, אביי's statement about שבועת ביטוי is refuted.

steps.title: אביי: the extra fifth for תרומה needs ignorance of the prohibition
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that everyone agrees a person pays חומש for eating תרומה only if he did not know the prohibition itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: Everyone agrees about תרומה that one is not liable to pay the added fifth unless he was unaware of its prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement of אביי about a non-כהן who eats תרומה by mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-כהן who eats תרומה unknowingly repays it plus a fifth (חומש). אביי says that to count as a mistake, he must not have known that eating תרומה is forbidden. Not knowing only the punishment is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: The priestly portion of produce, forbidden to non-כהנים
The added fifth paid for unwittingly eating תרומה

phrases.english: And אביי said:
Everyone agrees regarding תרומה
that one is not liable for it to pay a fifth
until he is unwitting regarding its prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, parallel statement of אביי about what counts as שגגה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability for חומש on תרומה requires ignorance of the prohibition itself.

steps.title: Who is 'everyone'? רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view 'everyone agrees' is meant to include, and answers רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Everyone agrees' — who? רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clarifies which opinion אביי meant to include by saying 'everyone agrees.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן normally holds that not knowing about כרת is enough to count as שגגה, even if the person knew the act was forbidden. אביי is saying that even רבי יוחנן agrees that for תרומה, one must not know the prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יוחנן, who holds that ignorance of כרת counts as שגגה

phrases.english: 'Everyone agrees' — who?
רבי יוחנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the phrase 'הכל מודים' in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which dissenting opinion is included in 'everyone'?

steps.title: That is obvious: רבי יוחנן only spoke about כרת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that it is obvious רבי יוחנן agrees, since his rule only applies where there is כרת, and eating תרומה carries no כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious! רבי יוחנן spoke only where there is כרת. Where there is no כרת, he did not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's statement as unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's leniency is built on not knowing about כרת. A non-כהן eating תרומה is not punished with כרת, so of course רבי יוחנן's rule does not apply. Why did אביי need to say it?

keyTerms.meaning: Spiritual 'cutting off,' a severe heavenly punishment

phrases.english: It is obvious!
When רבי יוחנן said it,
it was where there is כרת;
where there is no כרת, not!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for אביי's statement once 'everyone' is identified as רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's rule depends on כרת, which is absent with תרומה, so his agreement is self-evident.

steps.title: One might have treated death as equal to כרת
steps.stepSummary: אביי's point is needed because one might think מיתה בידי שמים takes the place of כרת, so ignorance of it would count. אביי teaches that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that death stands in place of כרת, so if he was unaware only of the death penalty, he should also be liable. So he teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'obvious' challenge by showing what mistake אביי's statement prevents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating תרומה on purpose is punished by מיתה בידי שמים. One might compare this to כרת and say that not knowing about the death penalty is enough for חומש. אביי teaches that this comparison does not hold: one must not know the prohibition itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Death at the hands of Heaven

phrases.english: You might have said:
death stands in place of כרת,
and when he was unwitting regarding death,
he should also be liable —
he teaches us (that it is not so).

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: מִיתָה בִּמְקוֹם כָּרֵת עוֹמֶדֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'פשיטא' challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the statement teaches a non-obvious point (מהו דתימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מיתה equals כרת, so ignorance of מיתה would count as שגגה for חומש.
steps.terutzMaskana: מיתה is not treated like כרת here; ignorance of the prohibition itself is required.

steps.title: רבא: death is like כרת, and חומש is like a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with אביי and holds that מיתה does stand in place of כרת, and חומש stands in place of a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Death stands in place of כרת, and the fifth stands in place of a sacrifice.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the opposite view: the comparison אביי rejected is actually correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, תרומה works the same way as a כרת sin with a קרבן. Not knowing about מיתה (or, per מונבז-style reasoning, about the חומש) can be enough to count as שגגה. This is a direct disagreement with אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: רבא, a contemporary of אביי who often disputes him

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: for תרומה, one must not know the prohibition itself; ignorance of מיתה is not enough. רבא: מיתה parallels כרת and חומש parallels קרבן, so the usual rules of שגגה carry over.

phrases.english: רבא said:
death stands in place of כרת
and the fifth stands in place of a sacrifice.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: מִיתָה בִּמְקוֹם כָּרֵת עוֹמֶדֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes אביי's position from steps 7–10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מיתה is equivalent to כרת and חומש is equivalent to a קרבן for defining שגגה.

steps.title: רב הונא: a lost traveler counts six days, then keeps שבת
steps.stepSummary: A person who lost track of the days counts six days and then observes the seventh as שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: If one was traveling on the road or in the desert and does not know when שבת is, he counts six days and keeps one day.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins: what a traveler does when he no longer knows which day is שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא says the first six days after he realizes he is lost are treated as weekdays. Then he keeps the seventh day as שבת.

phrases.english: רב הונא said:
If one was walking on the road or in the desert
and does not know when שבת is,
he counts six days
and observes one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: הָיָה מְהַלֵּךְ בַּדֶּרֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic, unrelated to the שגגה discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Count six days, then keep the seventh as שבת.

steps.title: חייא בר רב: keep שבת first, then count six
steps.stepSummary: חייא בר רב holds that the traveler keeps the very first day as שבת and then counts six weekdays.
steps.simpleTranslation: חייא בר רב says: He observes one day and then counts six.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives the opposite order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חייא בר רב, the traveler immediately treats the first day as שבת. After that he counts six weekdays before the next שבת.

phrases.english: חייא בר רב says:
He observes one day, and counts six.

steps.triggerLanguage: חִיָּיא בַּר רַב אוֹמֵר: מְשַׁמֵּר יוֹם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes רב הונא's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Keep the first day as שבת, then count six days.

steps.title: What is the root of their argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what underlying idea divides רב הונא and חייא בר רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up an explanation of the reasoning behind each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both rulings are clear. The גמרא now looks for the principle that leads each to his order of days.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the dispute in steps 12–13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle behind each opinion.

steps.title: Creation of the world versus אדם הראשון
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא follows the order of creation (six days, then שבת). חייא בר רב follows אדם הראשון, whose first full day was שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds like the creation of the world, and the other holds like אדם הראשון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the model each אמורא is using.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The world was created over six days and then came שבת, so רב הונא counts six and then rests. אדם הראשון was created on the sixth day, so his first full day was שבת, followed by six weekdays. That is why חייא בר רב rests first.

phrases.english: One master holds like the creation of the world,
and one master holds like Adam, the first man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב הונא models the order on creation; חייא בר רב models it on אדם הראשון's experience.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to support רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the traveler 'keeps one day for six,' which seems to mean six days first and then שבת, against חייא בר רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: If one was traveling and does not know when שבת is, he keeps one day for six. Does this not mean he counts six and then keeps one?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge חייא בר רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'one day for six' sounds as if the six come first and the day of rest comes after them. That matches רב הונא and would refute חייא בר רב.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
If one was walking on the road
and does not know when שבת is,
he observes one day for six.
Does it not mean
he counts six and observes one day?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges חייא בר רב from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording 'one day for six' implies the six weekdays come first, as רב הונא says.

steps.title: The ברייתא can be read either way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'one day for six' can also mean keeping one day first and then counting six.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means he keeps one day and then counts six.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends חייא בר רב by reading the ברייתא his way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only teaches the ratio of one rest day to six weekdays. It does not say which comes first, so it does not prove רב הונא right.

phrases.aramaic: לָא, מְשַׁמֵּר יוֹם אֶחָד וּמוֹנֶה שִׁשָּׁה.
phrases.english: No, he observes one day and counts six.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, מְשַׁמֵּר יוֹם אֶחָד וּמוֹנֶה שִׁשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Deflects the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'One day for six' means six weekdays first, then שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase can mean שבת first, then six days, so it fits חייא בר רב.

steps.title: The wording does not fit the new reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the answer in step 17. If the ברייתא meant 'keep one day, then count six,' it should have said exactly that.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does it say 'he keeps one day for six'? It should have said 'he keeps one day and counts six.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave for חייא בר רב. The wording 'for six' does not sound like 'first one day, then six.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 claimed that 'one day for six' could mean שבת comes first. Here the גמרא says that if the ברייתא meant that, it would have said 'keeps one and counts six.' The word 'for' suggests the one day comes as a result of the six, which means after them.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your reading is correct)

phrases.english: If so, why 'he keeps one day for six'?
'He keeps one day and counts six'
is what it should have said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the תירוץ of step 17 by pointing to the precise wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading in step 17 that 'one day for six' means one day first, then six.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase 'for six' does not naturally express 'one, then six.' That idea would be phrased 'keeps one and counts six.'

steps.title: A second ברייתא says count six first
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא states clearly that the traveler counts six days and then keeps one. This directly contradicts חייא בר רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And also, a ברייתא teaches: if someone was traveling on the road or in the desert and does not know when שבת is, he counts six days and keeps one day. This is a refutation of רבי חייא בר רב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, stronger challenge. A ברייתא that leaves no room for reinterpretation says six days come first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא could perhaps be read either way. This one says outright 'counts six, then keeps one.' That is exactly the view of רב הונא and the opposite of חייא בר רב.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
A refutation, a strong challenge from a תנאי source

phrases.english: And furthermore, it was taught:
If he was walking on the road or in the desert
and does not know when שבת is,
he counts six and keeps one day.
This is a refutation of רבי חייא בר רב!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, explicit source against חייא בר רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: חייא בר רב's view that the traveler keeps שבת on the first day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly orders the days as six first, then שבת.

steps.title: חייא בר רב is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the challenge. חייא בר רב's view is rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is indeed a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it has no answer. חייא בר רב's position is rejected, so the law follows רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the גמרא repeats the word 'תיובתא' as its own answer, it means the view has been knocked down. The traveler counts six days, and only then keeps שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: The final הלכה: a lost traveler counts six weekdays first, then keeps the seventh as שבת (like רב הונא).

phrases.english: It is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the refutation from step 19.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: חייא בר רב is refuted; count six days first, then keep שבת.

steps.title: רבא: work only for survival, except on that day
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that the lost traveler may only do enough work each day to feed himself, and not on the day he treats as שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Every day he does enough work for his food, except for that day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new topic: how much work the lost traveler is allowed to do. His first version says he works only for basic needs, and not at all on his chosen שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since any day might really be שבת, he cannot do normal work. He may do only what he needs to stay alive. This version also adds that on the day he set aside as שבת, he does no work at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Livelihood; here, the food he needs to survive
That day (the one he designated as שבת)

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּכָל יוֹם וָיוֹם עוֹשֶׂה לוֹ כְּדֵי פַרְנָסָתוֹ
phrases.english: Each and every day he makes enough for his sustenance
[except for that day].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new practical question about how the lost traveler behaves day to day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Work only for survival each day; no work on the designated day.

steps.title: Should he starve on that day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if he does no work on his chosen שבת, how will he eat that day?
steps.simpleTranslation: And on that day, should he die?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's 'except for that day.' Without any work, he would have no food for that day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This traveler has no food stored up and must work for each day's food. Forbidding all work on one day leaves him with nothing to eat. That cannot be the rule.

phrases.english: And on that day, should he die?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the exception in רבא's rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A total ban on work that day leaves him without food, which endangers his life.

steps.title: He prepares double the day before
steps.stepSummary: The answer: on the day before, he prepares two days' worth of food.
steps.simpleTranslation: He makes two portions of food the day before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that he prepares extra food the day before his chosen שבת, so he will have food on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is similar to a regular Friday, when we prepare food for שבת. The extra day's food solves the starvation problem.

phrases.english: He makes two portions of food the day before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the starvation objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical clarification of how the rule works
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No work on that day means no food.
steps.terutzMaskana: He prepares a double portion the day before.

steps.title: But the day before might be the real שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the day before might itself be the true שבת, so making double food then would be worse.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps yesterday was שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer from step 23. Doing extra work on a day that might be the real שבת is a bigger problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not actually know which day is שבת. Cooking double on the day before risks doing extra, unnecessary work on the real שבת, and for the sake of another day. Survival allows only one day's needs, not two.

phrases.english: But perhaps yesterday was שבת!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the double-portion answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of preparing two portions the day before.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Any day could be the real שבת, so extra work on the day before is not permitted.

steps.title: Revised rule: survival work every day, even that day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewrites רבא's rule: he does only survival-level work every day, including his chosen שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, every day he makes enough for his food, even on that day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the 'except for that day' version. It concludes that he works just enough to eat every single day, including his chosen שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since every day is equally doubtful, all seven days are treated the same: only enough work to stay alive. The designated שבת gets no special ban on survival work.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the chosen day is a total day of rest. Even on it he does survival work. It differs from the other days only by קידוש and הבדלה.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כָּל יוֹם וָיוֹם עוֹשֶׂה לוֹ פַּרְנָסָתוֹ,
phrases.english: Rather, each and every day he makes his sustenance,
even on that day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כָּל יוֹם וָיוֹם עוֹשֶׂה לוֹ פַּרְנָסָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the earlier version of רבא's statement after it was challenged.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No work on that day, with double food prepared the day before.
steps.terutzMaskana: Survival work every day, including that day.

steps.title: So how is that day different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what marks the chosen שבת as special if he works on it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that day, how is it recognizable to him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. If he works on his chosen שבת like any other day, what makes it שבת?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the work rules are the same every day, it seems the designated day has nothing special. The גמרא wants to know how he still marks it.

phrases.english: And that day, by what is it recognized for him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up question about the revised rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What distinguishes the designated שבת from the other days.

steps.title: קידוש and הבדלה mark the day
steps.stepSummary: The day is marked by saying קידוש at its start and הבדלה at its end.
steps.simpleTranslation: By קידוש and הבדלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that he marks his chosen שבת by reciting קידוש and הבדלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He cannot rest more on that day than on other days, but he can honor it with words. This keeps the memory of שבת alive for him.

keyTerms.meaning: קידוש, sanctifying the day at its start
הבדלה, separating the holy day at its end

steps.whatToRemember: The lost traveler does only survival work every day, and marks his chosen שבת with קידוש and הבדלה.

phrases.english: By kiddush and havdala.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קידוש and הבדלה distinguish the designated day.

steps.title: רבא: if he knows how many days since he left
steps.stepSummary: If the traveler knows how many days have passed since he left home, he may do full work on the weekday he left each week.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If he knows part of the information about the day he left (how many days ago it was), he may do work that whole day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second rule for a traveler with partial information. He knows how many days have passed, even though he does not know which weekday he left on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one sets out on a journey on שבת. So every seventh day counted from his departure (the 8th, 15th, and so on) is surely not שבת. On that day he may do any work, not just survival work.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיָה מַכִּיר מִקְצָת הַיּוֹם שֶׁיָּצָא בּוֹ,
phrases.english: If he partly knew the day on which he left,
he may do work the entire day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אִם הָיָה מַכִּיר מִקְצָת הַיּוֹם שֶׁיָּצָא בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new rule from רבא about a traveler with partial knowledge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Full work is permitted on the weekday of his departure.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא needed to say this, since it seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's rule as too obvious to need stating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows people do not start journeys on שבת. So the day he left was clearly a weekday. What did רבא add?

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious (a challenge asking what is new)

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what is new in step 28.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule seems self-evident, so stating it appears unnecessary.

steps.title: The point: the next day is not permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבא is needed to teach that only the departure weekday is permitted, not the day after, because people sometimes leave on Friday.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since a person does not leave on שבת, he also does not leave on ערב שבת. So if he left even on Thursday, let him be allowed to work two days. רבא teaches us that sometimes a person finds a caravan and happens to leave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the new point in רבא's words 'the whole day': only that one day. One might have thought the following day is also safe, but it is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mistaken logic: people avoid leaving on Friday too, so if he left he must have left by Thursday at the latest. Then the next weekday also could not be שבת. רבא rejects this, because a person sometimes joins a caravan that leaves on Friday. So the day after his departure weekday might really be שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces the mistaken assumption)
The fifth day of the week, Thursday

phrases.english: You might have said:
since he does not leave on Shabbat,
on Friday [also] he does not leave.

phrases.aramaic: וְהַאי, אִי נָמֵי בְּחַמְשָׁה בְּשַׁבְּתָא נָפֵיק
phrases.english: And this one, even if he left on Thursday,

phrases.aramaic: — לִישְׁתְּרֵי לֵיהּ לְמֶיעְבַּד מְלָאכָה תְּרֵי יוֹמֵי
phrases.english: should be permitted to do work two days.
He teaches us
that sometimes he finds a caravan
and it happens that he leaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge by naming the mistaken assumption that רבא excludes.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא, explaining the new point by naming a mistaken assumption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since people do not leave on Friday either, two days a week would be permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the departure weekday is permitted, since people sometimes leave on Friday with a caravan.

steps.title: Source for 'one who knows the עיקר שבת'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and asks for the Torah source of the rule about one who knows the עיקר שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One who knows the essence of שבת': from where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a phrase in the משנה. It asks for the source that separates one who forgot שבת entirely from one who knows about שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that one who forgot the עיקר שבת brings one חטאת for all his violations. One who knows the עיקר שבת brings a חטאת for each שבת. The גמרא wants the פסוק behind this difference.

keyTerms.meaning: The essence of שבת (that the מצוה of שבת exists)
From where are these matters derived?

phrases.english: One who knows the essence of Shabbat:
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from רבא's practical rules to the wording of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for the distinction regarding one who knows the עיקר שבת.

steps.title: Two פסוקים: singular and plural
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה points to two פסוקים. One says 'שבת' in the singular and one says 'שבתותי' in the plural.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: Two פסוקים are written. 'And the children of Israel shall keep the שבת,' and it is written, 'And My שבתות you shall keep.'
steps.whatsHappening: The answer begins by placing two פסוקים side by side. One uses the singular, the other the plural. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference between 'the שבת' (one) and 'My שבתות' (many) looks like a contradiction. The גמרא will use this difference to teach two different rules about קרבנות.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
Two verses are written:
'And the children of Israel shall keep the Shabbat,'
and it is written: 'And My Shabbatot you shall keep.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: תְּרֵי קְרָאֵי כְּתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to step 31 by presenting the two verses.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two verses, one singular and one plural, are the basis of the distinction.

steps.title: One observance for many, one for each
steps.stepSummary: The singular פסוק teaches one obligation covering many שבתות. The plural פסוק teaches a separate obligation for each שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? 'And the children of Israel shall keep the שבת': one observance for many שבתות. 'And My שבתות you shall keep': one observance for each and every שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the two פסוקים by giving each its own case. This provides the source for the משנה's two rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The singular teaches that sometimes many violations over many שבתות require only one חטאת. This applies to one who forgot the עיקר שבת. The plural teaches that sometimes each שבת requires its own חטאת. This applies to one who knows the עיקר שבת but forgot which day is שבת, since each שבת is a separate lapse in awareness.

keyTerms.meaning: Observance; here, one unit of obligation (one חטאת)

steps.whatToRemember: Singular 'שבת' = one חטאת for many שבתות (forgot the עיקר שבת). Plural 'שבתותי' = a חטאת for each שבת (knows the עיקר שבת).
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the Torah basis for the משנה's rule that the number of חטאות depends on what kind of forgetting happened.

phrases.english: How so?
'And the children of Israel shall keep the Shabbat'
means one observance for many Shabbatot.
'And My Shabbatot you shall keep'
means one observance for each and every Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer by reconciling the two verses.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The singular verse teaches one חטאת for many שבתות. The plural verse teaches a separate חטאת for each שבת.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק flips the reading of the two verses
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק argues the opposite reading makes more sense. The singular 'השבת' teaches a separate observance for each שבת. The plural 'שבתותי' teaches one observance for many שבתות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק challenged this: On the contrary, the opposite makes more sense! 'And the children of Israel shall keep the שבת' teaches one observance for each and every שבת. 'And you shall keep My שבתות' teaches one observance for many שבתות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק attacks the reading we just learned. He says each פסוק actually teaches the opposite of what we thought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier view said the singular word means one obligation for many שבתות. רב נחמן בר יצחק reads the singular 'the שבת' as pointing at each individual שבת on its own. He reads the plural 'My שבתות' as grouping many שבתות into one observance. He does not argue with the הלכה. He only switches which פסוק is the source for each rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it strongly (a forceful objection)
One observance (one obligation, which here means one חטאת)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב נחמן בר יצחק disagrees with the משנה's הלכה. Both views agree that one who forgets the עיקר שבת brings one חטאת for many שבתות, while one who knows the עיקר שבת (but forgot it was שבת) brings a separate חטאת for each שבת. Both also learn this from the same two פסוקים. They only argue about which פסוק teaches which half.
steps.whatToRemember: Both readings learn the משנה's rule from comparing the singular and plural פסוקים. The only argument is which פסוק teaches 'one for many' and which teaches 'one for each'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the source of the משנה's rule is secure either way. The two-פסוקים structure stands even though the exact assignment is debated.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקִיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak strongly objected to it:
On the contrary, the opposite is reasonable:
'And the children of Israel shall keep the Shabbat'
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק that says 'Shabbat' in the singular.

phrases.english: one observance for each and every Shabbat.
'And you shall keep My Shabbatot'
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק that says 'Shabbatot' in the plural.

phrases.english: one observance for many Shabbatot.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקִיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אַדְּרַבָּה אִיפְּכָא מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges and reverses the assignment of the two פסוקים given in Step 33.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading in Step 33, which assigned 'one for many' to the singular פסוק and 'one for each' to the plural פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The singular word 'השבת' more naturally points to each individual שבת. The plural 'שבתותי' more naturally groups many שבתות together. So the reverse reading is more logical.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה's case of one who knows it is שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה, 'one who knows that it is שבת', to begin discussing that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: 'One who knows that it is שבת.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes a new line. This is a setup step that prepares the next discussion about a person who knows it is שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the sugya dealt with the source for the cases of one who forgot the עיקר שבת and one who knows the עיקר שבת. Now the focus moves to the משנה's next case: someone who knows today is שבת but forgot that these מלאכות are forbidden. In that case he is liable for each אב מלאכה. The גמרא is about to explain this case.

phrases.english: One who knows that it is Shabbat.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה, opening a new topic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the source discussion and opens a new section by quoting the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה discusses one who knows it is שבת. The גמרא will now explain this case.
